# NGC 4449: Small Galaxy, Big Impact

Though our Milky Way stretches 100,000 light-years across with hundreds of billions of stars, the tiniest galaxies—like the dwarf galaxy NGC 4449 captured here by the Hubble Space Telescope—are ten times smaller and contain only a few billion stars, yet vastly outnumber their larger cousins throughout the universe. Surprisingly, these cosmic minnows are blowing away oxygen and other heavy elements into space through powerful stellar winds and explosions far more effectively than scientists expected, suggesting they may actually be crucial recyclers that scatter the building blocks of planets and life throughout the cosmos.
